﴿By the time (al-'asr)﴾ There are three views on this. The first is that it means the 'Asr prayer, by which Allah swears because of its excellence. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who misses the 'Asr prayer is as though he has been stripped of his family and his wealth." The second is that it means the late afternoon, by which He swears just as He swears by the forenoon (al-duha). This is supported by the words of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about al-'asr, and he said: 'Your Lord has sworn by the end of the day.'" The third is that it means time.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ "Mankind" (al-insan) is a generic term, and for that reason those who believe are excepted from it, so the exception is a connected one (istithna' muttasil).

﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ That is, they counsel one another to the truth and to patience. The truth is Islam and what it comprises, and in this there is an allusion to the falsehood of the disbelievers. In the mention of patience there is an allusion to the patience of the believers in the face of the harm the disbelievers inflicted on them in Mecca.
